title: Error stack trace exposed to end users
claim: Displaying the full stack trace in the UI potentially leaks internal implementation details (file paths, function names) to end users.
evidence: The catch block creates a stackDiv and sets its textContent to `Stack: ${e.stack}` without any condition or sanitization.
trigger: Any runtime error during initialization will cause the stack trace to be rendered in the game-container element, visible to the user.
impact: Information disclosure that could aid an attacker in targeting specific code paths or understanding application internals. Also degrades user experience by showing raw stack traces.
test_implication: End-to-end tests should verify that errors are displayed in a user-friendly manner without stack traces in production builds.
suggested_verification: Trigger an error during initialization and inspect the DOM to confirm stack trace is displayed; then check if this is acceptable in production environment.
suggested_fix: Remove or conditionally display stack trace only in debug mode (e.g., if DEBUG is true), or log to console only and show a generic error message to the user.

title: Missing check for already loaded document
claim: If the script executes after DOMContentLoaded has already fired (e.g., loaded with async or injected dynamically), the initialization code will never run, leaving the game uninitialized.
evidence: The script attaches a listener to DOMContentLoaded but does not check document.readyState. If readyState is 'interactive' or 'complete', the event will not fire again.
trigger: Including this script with an async attribute or loading it dynamically after page load.
impact: The game will not start; the container will remain empty or show default content, with no error visible.
test_implication: Tests should simulate loading the script after DOMContentLoaded to ensure initialization still occurs.
suggested_verification: Load the page with the script tag having async attribute and observe that game does not initialize.
suggested_fix: Replace the event listener with a ready state check, e.g., if (document.readyState === 'loading') { document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init); } else { init(); }

title: Assumes thrown exception has a stack property
claim: If a non-Error value is thrown (e.g., a string or number), the caught exception will not have a stack property, resulting in 'Stack: undefined' being displayed.
evidence: The code directly accesses e.stack without checking if e is an Error object or if stack is defined.
trigger: Any code throwing a non-Error value (e.g., throw 'failure';) will cause e.stack to be undefined.
impact: User sees 'Stack: undefined' in the error display, which is confusing but not harmful.
test_implication: Unit tests should cover non-Error throws to ensure graceful handling.
suggested_verification: Manually throw a string in the initialization code and observe the error display.
suggested_fix: Check if e instanceof Error or if e.stack is defined before using it; otherwise, omit the stack or use String(e).

title: Reliance on global constructors reduces modularity and testability
claim: The main entry point assumes GameModel, GameView, and GameController are globally defined, which may not hold in module-based builds and makes the code harder to test and reuse.
evidence: The code instantiates the classes directly without importing them, relying on global namespace.
trigger: If this file is used in a module bundler that does not expose these classes globally, a ReferenceError will occur (caught and displayed as error).
impact: Potential runtime failure in certain environments; also inhibits tree-shaking and static analysis.
test_implication: If testing this file in isolation, mocks must be injected globally, which is fragile.
suggested_verification: Attempt to bundle this file with a module system that does not expose globals and observe ReferenceError.
suggested_fix: Import the classes using ES modules or dependency injection to decouple this entry point from global state.

title: Game tokens may be hidden behind board cells due to missing z-index
claim: Tokens are absolutely positioned but have no z-index while .cell has z-index: 1, causing tokens to be stacked below cells.
evidence: CSS: .game-token { position: absolute; pointer-events: none; transition: left 250ms linear, top 250ms linear; } and .cell { position: relative; z-index: 1; }
trigger: When tokens are rendered as siblings of cells inside the board, they will be behind the cells.
impact: Tokens are invisible or partially obscured, breaking game visibility.
test_implication: Visual regression/testing needed to confirm token stacking.
suggested_verification: Inspect element in browser and verify computed stacking order; or add screenshot tests.
suggested_fix: Add z-index: 10 (or higher) to .game-token to ensure tokens appear above cells.

title: Active player highlight uses span selector while other player info styles target divs
claim: The rule #player-info div.active-player span:nth-child(2) likely fails because player info items use nested divs as styled by earlier rules, so the color highlight won't apply.
evidence: Earlier rules use #player-info div div div:nth-child(2) to style the name/score, but active player rule uses span:nth-child(2).
trigger: If the markup uses div elements for player info fields (as suggested by the CSS), the active player's text color will not change to yellow.
impact: Active player indication is missing or incorrect, reducing usability.
test_implication: Need to test active player state styling.
suggested_verification: Inspect active player element to see if color style applies; compare with HTML structure.
suggested_fix: Change selector to #player-info div.active-player div:nth-child(2) or use more consistent class/ID selectors.

title: Player info panel horizontally unpositioned due to missing left/right properties
claim: The panel is absolutely positioned with top:50% and transform: translateY(-50%) but no left or right, causing it to be placed according to its static position, likely not centered or overlaying the board as intended.
evidence: CSS: #player-info { position: absolute; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); ... } with no left/right.
trigger: When the game renders, the panel may appear at the left edge of the container or interfere with flex items.
impact: Layout is broken; player info may not be visible where expected.
suggested_verification: Open game and inspect location of player info panel.
suggested_fix: Add left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); or explicit left/right values to center or position as intended.

title: Game container overflows viewport between 601px and 800px
claim: The base styles set #game-container width: 800px, and the only max-width media query is 600px; viewports between 601px and 800px will cause horizontal scrolling because the container width remains 800px.
trigger: Viewing on devices with viewport width 601-800px (e.g., small tablets or landscape phones).
impact: Horizontal scrolling and poor user experience; content may be cut off.
suggested_verification: Use browser devtools to simulate viewport 700px and observe overflow.
suggested_fix: Adjust media query breakpoint to max-width: 800px or add intermediate breakpoints, or use max-width:100% on #game-container by default with a max-width of 800px.

title: Token movement transition overridden by move-to-board class
claim: The rule .game-token.move-to-board sets transition: transform, which replaces the base transition on left and top, disabling smooth movement when the class is applied.
evidence: Base .game-token has transition: left 250ms linear, top 250ms linear; .game-token.move-to-board has transition: transform 1.5s ease-in-out;
trigger: When a token has the move-to-board class and its left/top properties change, no animation occurs because the transition property is overridden.
impact: Token movement may appear jumpy or instantaneous, breaking intended animation.
test_implication: Test token movement animations with and without move-to-board class.
suggested_verification: Toggle class and change left/top via JS to observe if transition occurs.
suggested_fix: Specify transition for all relevant properties: transition: left 250ms linear, top 250ms linear, transform 1.5s ease-in-out;

title: Duplicate CSS rules for #game-board-container
claim: The selector #game-board-container is defined three times with identical or similar properties (flex: 1; position: relative), causing unnecessary duplication and potential confusion.
evidence: Occurrences at lines 256-258, 282-285, and inside media queries at 365-368 and 380-383.
trigger: Future edits may be made in one place but not others, leading to inconsistent styles.
impact: Maintenance overhead, higher risk of errors.
test_implication: No functional test needed; code quality review.
suggested_fix: Consolidate into one rule, remove duplicates, and use media queries only for overrides.

title: Footer fixed width 620px can overflow on small screens
claim: The footer has width: 620px and no responsive overrides; on viewports narrower than 620px it will cause horizontal overflow.
evidence: CSS: #app-footer { width: 620px; } no media query adjusts it.
trigger: Viewing on mobile devices with viewport <620px.
test_implication: Responsive testing needed on small screens.
suggested_fix: Change to max-width: 100%; width: auto; or add media query to reduce width.

title: Missing semantic landmarks and heading for page content
claim: The page lacks a main landmark and heading hierarchy, making it difficult for assistive technology users to navigate. The game title is presented as a div with class title-main instead of an <h1>, and content regions are divs without roles.
evidence: Lines 10-26 contain the main content wrapped in <div id="game-container">, but no <main> or <h1> is used. The title 'SANYALnet Labs Snakes & Ladders Arena' in line 14 is a <div class="title-main">.
trigger: A screen reader user tries to navigate by landmarks or headings; they will not find a main region or a top-level heading, and the game content will be announced as generic divs.
impact: Reduced accessibility and compliance with WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks). Users relying on assistive technology may have difficulty understanding page structure.
test_implication: Accessibility testing should verify that the page has a single main landmark and appropriate heading levels.
suggested_verification: Use a tool like axe or Lighthouse accessibility audit; check for 'Page must have a main landmark' and 'Heading levels should only increase by one'.
suggested_fix: Wrap the main game area in a <main> element, change the title div to an <h1> (or add an <h1> if the title should be separate). Use semantic elements for commentary and left panel as appropriate.

title: No placeholder or fallback content in game-board-container
claim: The #game-board-container div is empty and relies entirely on JavaScript to populate it. If any of the scripts fail to load or execute (e.g., network error, syntax error), the user sees a blank area with no error message, leading to a broken experience.
evidence:
Line 20:
; there is no static content, and the noscript element only covers disabled JavaScript, not script errors.
trigger: A user loads the page but one of the script files (gameModel.js, gameController.js, gameView.js, main.js) throws an error or returns 404; the container remains empty and no feedback is shown.
impact: Poor resilience and user experience; no indication of failure.
test_implication: Need to test scenario where scripts fail; verify that a fallback message appears or error handling is present.
suggested_verification: Manually block one script in DevTools or simulate a 404; observe that the board area is blank. Or add unit test for initialization failure.
suggested_fix: Add a static loading/error message inside #game-board-container, e.g., 'Loading game... If this message persists, please check your internet connection.' JavaScript can replace this content upon successful initialization. Alternatively, use window.onerror to display an error.

title: Inline styles used for noscript and footer link, harming maintainability
claim: Inline styles are used on the noscript div (line 28) and footer link (line 34), mixing presentation with content. This makes it harder to maintain and override styles, and violates separation of concerns.
evidence: Line 28: style="text-align: center; padding: 20px; background: #fff3cd; color: #856404; border: 1px solid #ffeeba;"; Line 34: style="font-size: 14px;".
trigger: A developer needs to change the warning appearance or the footer link size; they must edit the HTML rather than the CSS.
impact: Reduced maintainability; potential inconsistency if other styles are added.
test_implication: Not applicable to unit tests, but style consistency checks could flag inline styles.
suggested_verification: Run a code linter (e.g., stylelint with no-inline-styles) or grep for style=.
suggested_fix: Move these styles to CSS classes, e.g., .noscript-warning and .footer-link.
